payload.rebuttal: fixed: The test used the same message text (msg0..msgN) for every gate result in the fixture. lint (205 failures) and types (200 failures) share one attempt, and lint's own failure_ids come first, so the wrong version's attempt-wide query still returned lint's own first 200 rows when asked for lint's gate_result_id, and it was only the types block where the wrong version actually substitutes lint's rows for types' own rows. Because both gate results used identical message strings, that substitution produced the same msg0..msg199 list the correct code would have produced, so the assertion could not tell the two apart. I changed `_failures` to take a `tag` parameter and prefix every message with the owning gate's name (lint-msg0, types-msg0, tests-msg0), and updated the three call sites and assertions in tests/test_view_server.py accordingly. With the tag in place, the wrong version now makes the types block show lint-msg0..lint-msg199 instead of types-msg0..types-msg199, which fails the assertion. I confirmed this by hand-applying the exact SQL edit from the finding to saffron/view/server.py and re-running the test: it now fails with the wrong version applied and passes on HEAD. Committed as edd0046b.
